questions.topic: eGurukul · Hemolytic Anemia - Sickle Cell Disease
questions.stemHtml: A 10-year-old boy presents with severe pain in his bilateral hips, arms and diffuse body aches. He had similar episodes in the past but was never hospitalised. Laboratory investigations are normal except for a total bilirubin of 1.5 mg/dL and suggestive of microcytic anemia. His peripheral smear is shown. What is the most likely pathogenesis of the given condition?

options.label: A
options.text: A somatic mutation that causes deranged messenger RNA splicing of the globin gene.

options.label: C
options.text: Mutation in the β-globin gene that changes the sixth amino acid from glutamic acid to valine.

options.label: D
options.text: One of the four α-globin loci is deleted.
